sections.heading: Teach me how completely grace holds me
sections.text: Lord God, my Father, teach me to see that your grace is not just how my Christian life began. Your grace came before I ever came to you, stays with me now, and will carry me all the way home. You hold together every part of my salvation, and not one link in your saving work can snap or fail.
theological_themes: Grace as the source, sustainer, and completion of salvation
God's preserving work in the believer
Assurance grounded in God's action, not personal strength

scripture_references.connection: Paul presents God's saving purpose as an unbroken sequence from foreknowledge to glorification. This supports the prayer's confidence that grace precedes, accompanies, and completes salvation.
Paul's confidence rests in God finishing the good work he began in believers. That grounds the prayer's request to know that grace sustains the redeemed soul to the end.

sections.heading: Let the cross keep doing its deep work in me
sections.text: Everything I need comes to me through the cross of Jesus. Let that grace keep reaching into me: face my sin honestly, wash me clean, make my heart new, strengthen my will, pull my affections toward you, and light a real love for you in my soul. Let your grace rule the hidden places inside me, and make my thoughts, words, and work belong to you. Teach me, through Jesus, how immeasurably loved I am.
theological_themes: The cross as the fountain of cleansing and renewal
Grace that forgives and also transforms
Consecration of the whole inner life to God
Knowing God's love through Christ crucified

scripture_references.connection: This passage describes grace not only as saving but also as training believers to live godly lives, because Christ gave himself to redeem and purify a people for his own possession.
John connects fellowship with God and cleansing from sin directly to the blood of Jesus. This supports the prayer's claim that grace from the cross washes and restores.

sections.heading: Remembering what I have in Christ
sections.text: How rich I am in Jesus Christ. Apart from him, I would be far away from you, a stranger with no right to come close. In him, I am brought near and welcomed. Apart from him, I would be too guilty to lift my eyes. In him, I can look to you as my Father and my Friend. Apart from him, shame would shut my mouth. In him, I can speak freely to you, asking for what I need and praising you for who you are.
theological_themes: Access to God through Christ
Reconciliation from alienation to nearness
Adoption and confidence before the Father
Prayer made possible by Christ

scripture_references.connection: Paul contrasts being separated and far off with being brought near by the blood of Christ. This directly supports the prayer's movement from estrangement without Christ to nearness in him.
Because Jesus is the great high priest, believers are invited to draw near to God with confidence. This grounds the prayer's freedom to speak to God in petition and praise.
Paul teaches that believers have received the Spirit of adoption and can cry out to God as Father. This supports the prayer's confidence that God is not merely Judge but Father to those in Christ.

sections.heading: Resting in what Christ has closed and opened
sections.text: Apart from Christ, your holiness would be terrifying to me, and judgment would be all I could expect. In Christ, I find your love and the rest my soul needs. Apart from him, death and hell would stand open before me. In him, those doors are shut against me by his precious blood. Apart from him, the future would be darkness. In him, eternal glory stretches out ahead. Apart from him, every accusation against me would crush me. In him, those accusations are answered, and you give me joy and peace.
theological_themes: Deliverance from wrath and condemnation through Christ
Christ's blood as the believer's security
Hope of eternal glory
Peace of conscience because accusations are answered in Christ

scripture_references.connection: Paul declares that those who are in Christ Jesus are no longer under condemnation. This grounds the prayer's contrast between judgment apart from Christ and rest in him.

Paul answers every charge against God's people by pointing to God's justification and Christ's death, resurrection, and intercession. This supports the prayer's confidence that accusations lose their power in Christ.
Paul sets present affliction in light of eternal glory. This illuminates the prayer's hope that, in Christ, the believer's horizon is not darkness but glory.

sections.heading: Receiving everything else through him with thanks
sections.text: Apart from Jesus, even the good things around me would expose how badly I have used your gifts and how deserving of judgment I am. But in him, the things you place in my life become reasons for comfort, worship, and gratitude. Teach me to receive what you give with open hands, enjoy it rightly, and give thanks to you for it.
theological_themes: Created gifts received rightly through reconciliation with God
Thanksgiving as the proper response to God's provision
Providence interpreted through union with Christ

scripture_references.connection: Paul teaches that God's created gifts are to be received with thanksgiving and made holy by God's word and prayer. This supports the prayer's desire to enjoy outward blessings rightly before God.

Paul says God works all things for the good of those who love him and are called according to his purpose. This supports the prayer's confidence that, in Christ, the believer's circumstances are governed by God's saving care.

sections.heading: Praising you for Jesus
sections.text: So I praise you, Father, for grace. I praise you for the gift too great for words: Jesus himself, given for me and now my whole hope.
theological_themes: Thanksgiving for grace
Jesus Christ as God's indescribable gift
Christ as the believer's hope

scripture_references.connection: Paul ends his reflection on God's generosity with thanks for God's inexpressible gift. This provides a biblical frame for the prayer's final praise for Jesus and grace.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original uses strong language about wrath, hell, and eternal anguish. This adaptation preserves that theology while expressing it in contemporary language rather than softening it.

The line about external things ministering to comfort could be misunderstood as saying all circumstances are pleasant or materially beneficial. It has been rendered through the lens of providence, thanksgiving, and rightly receiving God's gifts, without implying a prosperity-gospel reading.
The prayer assumes an exclusivist Christian claim: apart from Christ there is alienation and judgment, while in Christ there is access to God, forgiveness, and eternal hope.
significant_interpretive_choices: The original's repeated contrast between 'without him' and 'in him' was retained as a major structural movement because it carries the prayer's central theological logic: every privilege comes through union with Christ.

The image of touching the kingly sceptre was rendered as being welcomed and allowed to draw near, supported by the biblical theme of access to God's throne through Christ rather than by a surface allusion to royal imagery.
The phrase 'every accusation is charmed into joy and peace' was interpreted as accusations being answered and silenced by Christ's justifying work, not as a magical or sentimental transformation.
